topic: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC (Question 1)
question: [Day 1 System Design: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC] Question 1: In the system architecture of System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC, how is horizontal scalability achieved under heavy traffic bursts?

options.text: Stateless application tiers behind load balancers with auto-scaling groups and distributed caching.
Upgrading to a single server with infinite RAM.
Dropping all incoming client requests immediately.
Storing all user passwords in plaintext.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Horizontal scalability relies on stateless application services that scale dynamically behind an Application Load Balancer, offloading read state to distributed caches (Redis/Memcached). (Focus: Day 1 System Design on System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC)

topic: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC (Question 2)
question: [Day 1 System Design: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC] Question 2: What is the primary distributed data consistency strategy applied in System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC?

options.text: Tunable quorums (W + R > N) or eventual consistency with asynchronous replication.
Single-threaded SQLite locking the whole database file on every read.
Ignoring all network partition failures.
Running all database queries inside client browsers.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Distributed architectures use tunable quorum replication or eventual consistency models to guarantee data durability without sacrificing availability during network partitions. (Focus: Day 1 System Design on System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC)

topic: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC (Question 3)
question: [Day 1 System Design: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC] Question 3: Which caching pattern is optimal to avoid cache stampede and stale reads in System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC?

options.text: Cache-Aside with probabilistic early expiration (XFetch) or mutex locking on cache misses.
Disabling caching completely across all nodes.
Setting cache TTL to 100 years.
Storing cache entries in browser cookies only.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Cache stampede is prevented by acquiring a distributed lock on cache miss or employing probabilistic early expiration algorithms to recompute warm keys asynchronously. (Focus: Day 1 System Design on System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC)

topic: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC (Question 4)
question: [Day 1 System Design: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC] Question 4: How does the system ensure high availability and disaster recovery in System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC?

options.text: Multi-region deployment with geo-DNS routing and automated health check failovers.
Hosting all services on a single desktop computer in an office.
Running backup scripts once every decade.
Restarting the server every hour.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. High availability requires active-active or active-standby deployments spanning multiple availability zones and regions with Route 53 or Cloudflare Geo-DNS failover. (Focus: Day 1 System Design on System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC)

topic: System Design Foundations: Latency, Throughput & CAP/PACELC (Question 5)

Upgrading to a single server with infinite RAM.
Dropping all incoming client requests immediately.
Storing all user passwords in plaintext.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Horizontal scalability relies on stateless application services that scale dynamically behind an Application Load Balancer, offloading read state to distributed caches (Redis/Memcached). (Focus: Day 25 System Design on Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3))

topic: Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3) (Question 12)
question: [Day 25 System Design: Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3)] Question 12: What is the primary distributed data consistency strategy applied in Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3)?

options.text: Tunable quorums (W + R > N) or eventual consistency with asynchronous replication.
Single-threaded SQLite locking the whole database file on every read.
Ignoring all network partition failures.
Running all database queries inside client browsers.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Distributed architectures use tunable quorum replication or eventual consistency models to guarantee data durability without sacrificing availability during network partitions. (Focus: Day 25 System Design on Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3))

topic: Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3) (Question 13)
question: [Day 25 System Design: Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3)] Question 13: Which caching pattern is optimal to avoid cache stampede and stale reads in Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3)?

options.text: Cache-Aside with probabilistic early expiration (XFetch) or mutex locking on cache misses.
Disabling caching completely across all nodes.
Setting cache TTL to 100 years.
Storing cache entries in browser cookies only.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Cache stampede is prevented by acquiring a distributed lock on cache miss or employing probabilistic early expiration algorithms to recompute warm keys asynchronously. (Focus: Day 25 System Design on Design Cloud Object Storage Service (Amazon S3))

topic: Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster) (Question 11)
question: [Day 29 System Design: Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster)] Question 11: In the system architecture of Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster), how is horizontal scalability achieved under heavy traffic bursts?

options.text: Stateless application tiers behind load balancers with auto-scaling groups and distributed caching.
Upgrading to a single server with infinite RAM.
Dropping all incoming client requests immediately.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. topic: Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster) (Question 12)
question: [Day 29 System Design: Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster)] Question 12: What is the primary distributed data consistency strategy applied in Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster)?

options.text: Tunable quorums (W + R > N) or eventual consistency with asynchronous replication.
Single-threaded SQLite locking the whole database file on every read.
Ignoring all network partition failures.
Running all database queries inside client browsers.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. topic: Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster) (Question 13)
question: [Day 29 System Design: Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster)] Question 13: Which caching pattern is optimal to avoid cache stampede and stale reads in Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster)?

options.text: Cache-Aside with probabilistic early expiration (XFetch) or mutex locking on cache misses.
Disabling caching completely across all nodes.
Setting cache TTL to 100 years.
Storing cache entries in browser cookies only.

detailedExplanation: Correct Answer: A. Correct: A. Cache stampede is prevented by acquiring a distributed lock on cache miss or employing probabilistic early expiration algorithms to recompute warm keys asynchronously. (Focus: Day 29 System Design on Design a Distributed Caching System (Redis Cluster))
